steps.message:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station T-16 (survey area T). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)

1 | 312.0 | 6.08 | 6.08

3 | 884.4 | 3.48 | 24.32
4 | 1280.2 | 10.95 | 35.27
5 | 4929.0 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as H-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: T-16
Curve type: A-type (resistivities increase monotonically with depth: 312.0 → 794.3 → 884.4 → 1280.2 → 4929.0 ohm-m — this does NOT match an H-type signature, which requires a low-resistivity layer sandwiched between two higher-resistivity layers. The file classification appears to be in error and should be corrected/re-checked before use.)

Aquifer depth: 0–6.08 m (Layer 1, 312.0 ohm-m) is the only relatively low-resistivity zone in this sequence and is the most probable water-bearing/saturated interval (likely weathered overburden or alluvium); underlying layers show progressively higher resistivity consistent with increasingly competent, less porous bedrock.

Recommendation: Because the on-file H-type classification is inconsistent with the actual resistivity trend, flag this VES for re-interpretation before finalizing design; in the meantime, plan initial drilling/casing through the 0–6.08 m zone as the primary target for shallow groundwater, and log carefully through the 6–35 m interval to confirm whether increasing resistivity reflects true bedrock rather than a missed low-resistivity aquifer unit.
